office_does: The sheriff runs the Kitsap County Sheriff's Office, the county's largest department and its chief law-enforcement agency, which patrols, investigates, makes arrests and serves court orders and warrants.
race_blurb: Open seat after Sheriff John Gese resigned in June 2026. KCSO patrol chief Brandon L. Myers (Prefers Democratic Party), a 23-year insider, faces King County deputy and retired Navy officer Rick Kuss (Prefers Republican Party), who argues for change from outside the office and pledges no new taxes while the county weighs a sales-tax increase.

candidates.summary: Kitsap County Sheriff's Office patrol chief with a 23-year career in the office, from Explorer Cadet to detective sergeant; endorsed by the outgoing and former sheriffs and the deputies' guild.
highlights: 23 years at KCSO; promoted to patrol chief in 2026 [S6][S7]
Founding member of the office's Crisis Intervention Team; supervised major-crime and child-abuse investigations [S1]
Says the office must be properly staffed, supported and equipped, and calls for restoring proper funding [S1][S5]
Emphasizes transparency, community trust and keeping party politics out of the office [S3]
Endorsed by Sheriff John Gese, retired Sheriff Gary Simpson, the Deputy Sheriff's Guild and the Kitsap County Democratic Committee [S2]

experience.basis: Runs on a 23-year career inside KCSO, now patrol chief, with endorsements from current and former sheriffs; not the incumbent.

spending.basis: Says the office must be properly staffed, supported and equipped, and calls for restoring proper funding for the Sheriff's Office.

candidates.summary: King County deputy sheriff and retired Navy lieutenant commander with a criminal-justice master's degree; lost the 2022 Kitsap sheriff race and now runs as an outside change candidate.
highlights: Would restore a regional drug task force and says he will not seek reelection if he does not [S3]
Pledges no new taxes, a budget review to cut waste and overtime control [S3]
Says 'Change needs to come from the outside' [S3]
Names protecting children from abuse, exploitation and drugs as his top priority [S1][S2]
Supports 'accountable diversion' with incarceration if mandatory treatment fails [S3]

experience.basis: Argues change must come from outside the office and that he is 'unburdened by its past'; has never held the office or worked at KCSO.

taxes.basis: Pledges not to seek new taxes to fix problems he attributes to wasteful spending, while calling taxation a last resort.

spending.basis: Would thoroughly review the office budget, cut waste, control overtime and redirect existing money to frontline priorities.

safety.basis: Leads with enforcement (drug task force, fentanyl traffickers, incarceration when mandatory treatment fails) alongside accountable diversion.
